edit.description: the skeleton annotates its literal with it

summary: Export the declaration schema's input type, and annotate the skeleton init writes with it, so a consumer's literal is authorable.
acceptance: a consumer annotating declaration.ts gets tsc refusal and completion, not load refusal alone.
tests: the declaration skeleton init writes typechecks against the package's exported input type
notes: `Declaration` is `z.infer`, so a defaulted field (`scopeWritesToEntry`) is required on the output side and `satisfies Declaration` will not compile over a literal. The input side is the authorable one, and the skeleton's own annotation is the export's consumer. tsc-in-test precedent: tests/cliJobVerbs.test.ts.

edit.description: the chain.ts skeleton, and the written list
the written chain.ts loads as a Chain

summary: Have `flume-harness init` write the chain.ts hop — the factory over the declaration beside it — so an adopted repo can tick.
acceptance: a repo flume-harness init adopted resolves a chain at <stateRoot>/chain.ts with no hand-written file.
tests: init writes a chain.ts applying the package factory to the declaration beside it
the chain.ts init writes loads through the engine's chain loader as a valid Chain
notes: The engine refuses a load with no `<configDir>/chain.ts`, so init leaves a repo one file short of a tick. The hop is three lines identical in every consumer — *Verbatim copying is the detector*. `spec/harness.md` *Adoption and upgrade* lists four artifacts; the fifth row is the human's. The existing skeleton test's tsx-over-shim probe drives the written file through the real loader.
